messages:
liam: Quick follow-up on the MHA layout RFC — leaning toward keeping QKV contiguous in memory (B, S, 3, H, D) vs interleaved per-head. Wanted to capture kernel implications and runtime heuristics.

maya: +1 to discussion. Main tradeoffs I see: contiguous QKV simplifies fused matmul+softmax kernels (single GEMM per QKV block) but increases memory move when extracting heads.

sam: Agree. Also NHWC (batch, seq, head, dim) gives good unit-stride for per-head kernels on GPU -> better coalescing. NCHW style (batch, head, seq, dim) helps for some conv-like fusions but less common here.

anika: Is there a perf number we can point to for NHWC vs NCHW? small seq vs long seq?

maya: Rough numbers from microbench: for seq<=64 NHWC wins ~10–25% for per-head softmax path. For seq>=512 difference shrinks; memory bandwidth dominates.

ryan: Contiguous QKV (QKV concatenated per token) reduces index math in kernels, but causes extra copy for KV cache when caching per-head. Interleaved QKV (Q,K,V per head stored together) avoids copies for KV cache but complicates fused QKV GEMM.

liam: So maybe runtime should pick layout based on path: hosted (latency SLOs small seq) -> NHWC + contiguous QKV; dedicated high-throughput long-seq -> interleaved? Can we detect cheaply?

sam: Yes. Heuristics: if seq*batch < 16000 use NHWC contiguous. Also check model head count and dtype. Use cheap runtime probe: run a 1-step matmul microkernel at startup to measure memory-bound vs compute-bound.

maya: Kernel changes: implement two variants for fused QKV->attn: one expects contiguous QKV and does a single big GEMM; another expects interleaved and does 3 smaller GEMMs or a strided GEMM. Need plan for codegen to pick kernels by layout flag.

ryan: Also need to consider KV cache layout for incremental decoding. If contiguous QKV, append entering tokens then transpose per-head on the fly? That is expensive. Alternative: keep cache in interleaved layout even if compute uses contiguous; add fast transpose kernel when filling cache.

anika: Re: alignment — we should enforce 128B alignment for row stride to keep tensor cores happy. Also pad head dim to multiples of 32/64 depending on dtype.

liam: Good. Action items?

maya: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with: kernel variants, runtime heuristic thresholds, cache-layout tradeoffs, and memory alignment rules. Will include perf tables and sample cmake flags.

sam: I'll add microbench harness and a tiny startup probe in infra. Also add telemetry: which layout chosen and perf numbers.

ryan: I'll prototype fast transpose kernel for cache filling (CUDA) and measure overhead.

anika: Can I help with unit tests? I can add randomized layout tests and correctness checks.

deploybot: CI pipeline queued for microbench PR — will report results when finished :rocket:

liam: Thanks — let's sync tomorrow after initial numbers. :thumbsup:
